title: Where it grows
subtitle: Salta and high altitude
objectives: Explain how altitude shapes its style

steps.title: Salta and Cafayate
steps.body: Torrontés Riojano grows best in the Calchaquí Valleys of Salta, in north-west Argentina, around Cafayate, at 1,700 to over 3,000 m, among the highest vineyards in the world. It's also grown in La Rioja, the province that gave it its name, and in Mendoza and San Juan.

steps.title: Altitude
steps.body: At such altitude, days are hot and sunny, with intense ultraviolet light, while nights are cold. Torrontés ripens fully, developing its aromas, but keeps acidity. The UV thickens skins, adding aroma compounds. Without altitude, in hot lowlands, Torrontés can be flabby, bitter and too alcoholic.
steps.highlight: Sun by day, cold at night

steps.explanation: Torrontés is at its best high in the north.

steps.title: Making it
steps.body: Winemakers keep Torrontés fresh: cool fermentation in steel, no oak, early bottling. Some pick earlier to reduce alcohol and bitterness. A few producers make oaked, late harvest or sparkling versions, but the fresh, dry style dominates.

options: Cold nights keep acidity while sun ripens aromas
steps.explanation: Altitude gives a large day and night swing, balancing ripeness and freshness.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Torrontés thrives in Salta's high valleys, around Cafayate
Altitude keeps acidity while sun ripens aromas
